metadata.name: Minarchism (Nozick, 1974)
metadata.description: The rights-based minimal-state argument in Anarchy, State, and Utopia.
metadata.scope: The rights-based minimal-state argument in Anarchy, State, and Utopia. Scope excludes Nozick’s later revisions and other broader uses of the term libertarianism. No incumbent government is claimed to implement this doctrine completely. Strict revision-2 re-audit: assess only source-supported positions on the exact questions. Unsupported empirical comparisons, modern technology analogies and institutional particulars remain unknown. Absence of doctrine is not a neutral position. This draft must not be used to calculate or publish a complete profile. The 1974 minimal-state argument does not by itself prescribe universal suffrage, representative elections or a particular parliamentary constitution.
metadata.phrase: A society whose government is limited to protecting people and property, enforcing contracts and providing courts and defence.
